# Gateway responsibility and safe routing changes

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `architecture-api-gateway` · **Architecture & Distributed Systems** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S04-Q015](#S04-Q015)

<p>What responsibilities would you assign to an API gateway or reverse proxy, and what would remain in downstream services? How does the scope change when the component also provides API management?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Define and verify a gateway boundary that supports routing changes without taking over domain ownership.</p>

<ul>
<li>Assign gateway, reverse-proxy and API-management concerns to explicit owners.</li>
<li>Trace a request from route matching to the intended destination.</li>
<li>Design validation and recovery for configuration changes across replicas.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Request pipeline, middleware and filters](aspnet-request-pipeline.md)

<p>Begin with who owns request handling. Follow one route to understand the configuration contract, then change that route safely and challenge whether a proposed policy belongs in the gateway or the domain service.</p>

### S04-Q015 · Foundation

<a id="S05-Q024"></a>

<p>What responsibilities would you assign to an API gateway or reverse proxy, and what would remain in downstream services? How does the scope change when the component also provides API management?</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q015](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q015) · [S05-Q024](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q024)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q015](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q015)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What responsibilities belong in an API Gateway or reverse proxy?

</div>

**[S05-Q024](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q024)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain API management/gateway responsibilities.

</div>

**Why these source prompts share a canonical question:** Shared gateway responsibility contract; retain reverse-proxy and API-management contexts.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare request forwarding with broader API policy and lifecycle concerns. Establish the boundary before naming a gateway product.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Define gateway responsibility without centralizing all application behavior.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>The source includes reverse-proxy and API-management contexts. Clarify required capabilities; do not assume every product implements the same features.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Assign responsibility and ownership for a request policy and a domain rule.</li>
<li>Explain a centralization cost and how the boundary can be tested.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating reverse proxy, gateway and API management as identical feature sets.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Which check must a service still own if traffic can bypass the gateway?</li>
<li>What would you check before moving a policy into a managed gateway?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q016"></a>

### S04-Q016 · Mechanism

<p>What configuration would a gateway need to route an incoming request to the intended downstream service? Walk through one route and explain how you would verify it.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q016](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q016)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q016](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q016)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What configuration is typically required to route requests to downstream services?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Trace how the request is matched, transformed if necessary and forwarded. Explain the contract between the public endpoint and the destination.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Make routing behavior inspectable from configuration to destination.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify gateway product/version, environment and downstream protocol. Consult its official documentation before claiming syntax, precedence or defaults.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace a request using explicit matching and destination assumptions.</li>
<li>Test both the intended route and an ambiguous or unmatched request.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Listing a destination URL without explaining how the incoming request selects it.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you detect two routes that overlap unexpectedly?</li>
<li>Which forwarded request details does the downstream service require?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q017"></a>

### S04-Q017 · Application

<p>How would you allow routing or gateway configuration to change without redeploying the gateway for every change? Explain how the change would be validated, applied and recovered if it is wrong.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q017](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q017)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q017](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q017)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How can routing/configuration change without tightly coupling every change to a gateway redeployment?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>The goal is reducing deployment coupling, not removing control over configuration. Describe ownership and the sequence of a safe update.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design a controlled configuration-change path.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Identify gateway product/version and its supported update mechanisms in official documentation. Clarify who can publish changes and whether replicas update together.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Separate configuration ownership from executable deployment while retaining validation.</li>
<li>Account for inconsistent replica configuration and a recoverable bad update.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming external configuration makes changes automatically safe or immediately consistent.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What should happen if the configuration source is temporarily unavailable?</li>
<li>How would you find replicas still using an old route?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q018"></a>

### S04-Q018 · Trade-offs

<p>Which business concerns should remain outside the gateway? Use one proposed gateway change to explain where routing or policy ends and domain behavior begins.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q018](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q018)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q018](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q018)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Which concerns should not become business logic inside the gateway?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Domain behavior determines a business outcome; routing and policy govern request handling. The question asks you to defend the responsibility boundary.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Evaluate whether a gateway change creates business coupling.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a generic API; clarify whether traffic also enters through internal or non-HTTP paths and who owns the business rule.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explain the effect of the placement on ownership and independent change.</li>
<li>Show how the rule stays consistent across entry points and how to verify it.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Putting a rule in the gateway solely because every current request passes through it.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What happens to this rule when a message consumer invokes the same operation?</li>
<li>When would response aggregation be appropriate without moving domain ownership?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>An ASP.NET Core API has two backend versions behind a gateway. Design a routing change for one endpoint while other endpoints remain available. Define validation, replica consistency and rollback observations; explain who should enforce a business eligibility rule when internal calls can bypass the gateway.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Names gateway functions and can trace a simple route.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defends policy ownership and explains safe change, inconsistent replicas and recovery with concrete checks.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>Feature lists without a request trace or an observable configuration-change test do not establish the proposed boundary.</p>
